accepted.s: The Bharat Stage-I emission norms, popularly known as “India 2000”, were implemented throughout India from:
accepted.x: BS-I, also called India 2000, was implemented nationwide from 1 April 2000.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive label “India 2000” to identify the implementation year.
accepted.sec: Bharat Stage norms - nationwide implementation year

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the first implementation of Bharat Stage-II norms?
accepted.x: BS-II was introduced in Delhi from 1 April 2000 and was extended nationwide in 2005.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first-city date from the later nationwide date.
accepted.sec: Bharat Stage norms - nationwide implementation year

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the implementation of Bharat Stage norms:
1. BS-III was introduced in the NCR and ten big cities, including Hyderabad-Secunderabad, from 1 April 2005.
2. BS-III became applicable nationwide in 2010.
3. BS-IV was implemented nationwide in April 2017.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. BS-III began in the NCR and ten major cities in 2005, became nationwide in 2010, and BS-IV became nationwide in April 2017.
accepted.tq: Track the distinction between initial city coverage and nationwide implementation.
accepted.sec: Bharat Stage norms - nationwide implementation year

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: BS-IV was implemented nationwide in April 2017, not in 2010. Nationwide BS-III implementation occurred in 2010.
accepted.tq: Check the nationwide dates rather than the first-city dates.
accepted.sec: Bharat Stage norms - nationwide implementation year

accepted.s: The Bharat Stage emission norms are notified under the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 by which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
accepted.x: The norms are notified under the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, on the advice of CPCB and MoEFCC.
accepted.tq: Apply the “who would do this job?” method to identify the notifying authority.
accepted.sec: Bharat Stage norms - nationwide implementation year

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about tractor emission norms is correct?
1. Tractor norms were first notified in 1999.
2. Trem Stage II commenced on 1 June 2003.
3. Trem Stage III commenced on 1 October 2005.
accepted.x: The first tractor norms were notified in 1999; Trem Stage II began on 1 June 2003 and Trem Stage III on 1 October 2005.
accepted.tq: Combine closely related dates and eliminate an option by checking each date.
accepted.sec: Bharat Stage norms - nationwide implementation year

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly shows the equivalence between Bharat Stage and Euro norms?
o: BS-I—Euro II; BS-II—Euro III; BS-III—Euro IV; BS-IV—Euro V
BS-I—Euro I; BS-II—Euro II; BS-III—Euro III; BS-IV—Euro IV
BS-I—Euro I; BS-II—Euro III; BS-III—Euro IV; BS-IV—Euro VI
BS-I—Euro II; BS-II—Euro IV; BS-III—Euro V; BS-IV—Euro VI
accepted.x: BS-I, BS-II, BS-III and BS-IV correspond respectively to Euro I, Euro II, Euro III and Euro IV.
accepted.tq: Start from the sequential equivalence and reject shifted pairings.
accepted.sec: Euro norms equivalence and first adoption under the Bharat Stage name

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the relationship between Indian and European emission norms is correct?
o: India generally preceded Europe by about five years.
India adopted Euro norms only after BS-VI.
India and Europe adopted every norm in the same year.
India generally lagged Europe by about five years.
accepted.x: India generally lagged Europe by approximately five years in adopting equivalent emission standards.
accepted.tq: Watch for the reversed-comparison trap involving “preceded” and “lagged”.
accepted.sec: Euro norms equivalence and first adoption under the Bharat Stage name

accepted.s: Euro I norms began in Europe in which year?
accepted.x: Euro I began in Europe in 1992. The adoption of Euro II in Delhi on 1 April 2000 was a later Indian development.
accepted.tq: Separate the European commencement year from the Indian implementation year.
accepted.sec: Euro norms equivalence and first adoption under the Bharat Stage name

accepted.s: Which Bharat Stage was skipped when India transitioned from BS-IV to BS-VI?
accepted.x: India skipped BS-V and moved directly from BS-IV to BS-VI.
accepted.tq: Use the first/last distinction: BS-V is the only stage skipped by India.
accepted.sec: Transition BS-IV to BS-VI - stage skipped and why, SC deadline

accepted.s: The decision to leapfrog from BS-IV to BS-VI was taken in:
accepted.x: The decision to skip BS-V and leapfrog to BS-VI was taken in 2016.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the decision year from the implementation and court-order years.
accepted.sec: Transition BS-IV to BS-VI - stage skipped and why, SC deadline

accepted.s: The principal rationale for moving directly from BS-IV to BS-VI was to:
o: eliminate the need for refinery modifications
reduce the number of vehicle manufacturers in India
address urgent urban air pollution and close the gap with Europe in one step
replace all petrol vehicles with electric vehicles
accepted.x: The leapfrog was intended to address urgent urban air pollution, particularly in the Delhi-NCR region, and to close the technology gap with Europe without two successive changeovers.
accepted.tq: Match the policy decision with its stated environmental and technological objective.
accepted.sec: Transition BS-IV to BS-VI - stage skipped and why, SC deadline

accepted.s: The Supreme Court order concerning BS-IV vehicles provided that, from 1 April 2020:
o: BS-IV vehicles could be sold but not registered anywhere
only diesel BS-IV vehicles would be prohibited
BS-IV vehicles could neither be sold nor registered
only the manufacture of BS-IV vehicles would be prohibited
accepted.x: The Supreme Court ordered that no BS-IV vehicle could be sold or registered from 1 April 2020.
accepted.tq: Do not confuse the separate actions of sale and registration; both were covered.
accepted.sec: Transition BS-IV to BS-VI - stage skipped and why, SC deadline

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. BS-VI became applicable to all new vehicles from 1 April 2020.
2. Registering authorities may register non-compliant vehicles after a new emission norm takes effect.
3. The Supreme Court order on BS-IV vehicles was issued in 2018.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because registering authorities cannot register non-compliant vehicles after a norm takes effect.
accepted.tq: Identify the false statement by testing the authority’s legal limitation.
accepted.sec: Transition BS-IV to BS-VI - stage skipped and why, SC deadline

accepted.s: Which pollutant binds with haemoglobin to form carboxyhaemoglobin and thereby reduces oxygen supply to the body?
accepted.x: Carbon monoxide binds with haemoglobin to form carboxyhaemoglobin and impairs oxygen transport.
accepted.tq: Link the pollutant with its characteristic physiological mechanism.
accepted.sec: Vehicular pollutants - health effects

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes nitrogen oxides emitted by vehicles?
o: They are harmless unless combined with lead.
They primarily cause leukaemia by direct genetic mutation.
They affect only the nervous system and do not participate in atmospheric reactions.
They cause respiratory illness, contribute to ground-level ozone and may cause acid rain.
accepted.x: NOx causes respiratory illness, particularly affecting children, and contributes to ground-level ozone formation and acid rain.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that combines the pollutant’s health and environmental effects.
accepted.sec: Vehicular pollutants - health effects

accepted.s: Particulate matter of size PM2.5 is especially harmful because it:
o: penetrates deep into the lungs and bloodstream
is rapidly converted into harmless oxygen
remains confined to the upper atmosphere
accepted.x: PM2.5 can penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream, contributing to heart and lung disease.
accepted.tq: Use the particle-size implication to identify the deeper penetration effect.
accepted.sec: Vehicular pollutants - health effects

accepted.s: Which pollutant is specifically associated with carcinogenicity and leukaemia?
accepted.x: Benzene is a carcinogenic pollutant associated with leukaemia.
accepted.tq: Match the pollutant with its distinctive disease association.
accepted.sec: Vehicular pollutants - health effects

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about lead pollution:
1. Lead is a neurotoxin.
2. Lead exposure can harm the brain development of children.
3. Leaded petrol was phased out in India by 2000.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Lead damages the nervous system, is particularly harmful to children’s brain development, and leaded petrol was phased out in India by 2000.
accepted.tq: Treat the date and the health effects as separate statements to be verified.
accepted.sec: Vehicular pollutants - health effects

accepted.s:
Which of the following pollutants are included among those covered by Euro emission norms?
1. Carbon monoxide
2. Hydrocarbons
3. Lead
accepted.x: The covered list includes carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons and lead; therefore all three are correct.
accepted.tq: Prefer the inclusive option when all listed pollutants belong to the regulated set.
accepted.sec: Vehicular pollutants - health effects

accepted.s:
Arrange the fuel-sulphur limits under the following Bharat Stage norms in descending order:
A. BS-VI
B. BS-II
C. BS-IV
D. BS-III
accepted.x: The limits descend as BS-II—500 ppm, BS-III—350 ppm, BS-IV—50 ppm and BS-VI—10 ppm.
accepted.tq: Arrange numerical values from the highest to the lowest rather than relying only on stage order.
accepted.sec: Pollutants regulated - CO, NOx, HC, PM limits; fuel sulphur per stage

accepted.s: The fuel-sulphur limit under BS-IV was reduced to:
accepted.x: BS-IV fuel had a sulphur limit of 50 ppm. The BS-VI limit was further reduced to 10 ppm.
accepted.tq: Separate the closely spaced 50 ppm and 10 ppm values.
accepted.sec: Pollutants regulated - CO, NOx, HC, PM limits; fuel sulphur per stage

accepted.s: Euro II ultra-low sulphur diesel refers to diesel containing:
o: 0.005% sulphur or less, equivalent to 50 ppm
0.05% sulphur or less, equivalent to 500 ppm
0.001% sulphur or less, equivalent to 10 ppm
0.5% sulphur or less, equivalent to 5,000 ppm
accepted.x: Euro II ultra-low sulphur diesel contains 0.05% sulphur or less, which is equivalent to 500 ppm.
accepted.tq: Convert percentage to parts per million before selecting the answer.
accepted.sec: Pollutants regulated - CO, NOx, HC, PM limits; fuel sulphur per stage

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the BS-I emission limits?
o: CO: 2.72–6.90 mg/km; HC+NOx: 0.97–1.70 mg/km; diesel PM: 0.14–0.25 mg/km
CO: 0.97–1.70 g/km; HC+NOx: 2.72–6.90 g/km; diesel PM: 0.01–0.05 g/km
CO: 2.72–6.90 g/km; HC+NOx: 0.97–1.70 g/km; diesel PM: 0.14–0.25 g/km
accepted.x: The BS-I limits were CO 2.72–6.90 g/km, HC+NOx 0.97–1.70 g/km and diesel PM 0.14–0.25 g/km.
accepted.tq: Check both the numerical ranges and the units before choosing.
accepted.sec: Pollutants regulated - CO, NOx, HC, PM limits; fuel sulphur per stage

accepted.s: Which statement regarding BS-VI emission limits is correct?
o: BS-VI retained the BS-IV fuel-sulphur limit of 50 ppm.
The NOx limit is 80 mg/km for petrol and 60 mg/km for diesel vehicles.
The NOx limit is 60 mg/km for petrol and 80 mg/km for diesel vehicles.
The diesel PM limit is 45 mg/km.
accepted.x: The BS-VI NOx limits are 60 mg/km for petrol and 80 mg/km for diesel vehicles; the diesel PM limit is 4.5 mg/km and fuel sulphur is 10 ppm.
accepted.tq: Watch for reversed petrol-diesel values and misplaced decimal points.
accepted.sec: Pollutants regulated - CO, NOx, HC, PM limits; fuel sulphur per stage

accepted.s: The expected reduction in NOx emissions under BS-VI is approximately:
o: 25% for petrol cars and 70% for diesel cars
50% for both petrol and diesel cars
10% for petrol cars and 20% for diesel cars
70% for petrol cars and 25% for diesel cars
accepted.x: BS-VI is expected to reduce NOx emissions by about 25% in petrol cars and 70% in diesel cars.
accepted.tq: Use the fuel-type comparison and avoid reversing the two percentages.
accepted.sec: Pollutants regulated - CO, NOx, HC, PM limits; fuel sulphur per stage

accepted.s: In a diesel vehicle, Selective Catalytic Reduction primarily:
o: traps soot and stores it permanently
converts carbon monoxide into carbon dioxide without a catalyst
monitors emission performance and alerts the driver
converts NOx into nitrogen and water using a urea solution
accepted.x: SCR uses a urea solution such as AdBlue to convert diesel NOx into nitrogen and water.
accepted.tq: Match the technology with its specific emission-control function.
accepted.sec: BS-VI technologies - DPF, SCR, OBD, RDE

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the principal function of a Diesel Particulate Filter?
o: Converting NOx into nitrogen and water
Trapping soot and periodically oxidising it
Increasing the sulphur content of fuel
accepted.x: A DPF traps soot and periodically oxidises the accumulated particulate matter.
accepted.tq: Distinguish particulate control by DPF from NOx control by SCR.
accepted.sec: BS-VI technologies - DPF, SCR, OBD, RDE

accepted.s: OBD-II in a BS-VI vehicle is intended to:
o: carry out only laboratory-based emission testing
measure only fuel quality at the refinery
continuously monitor emission performance and alert the driver
accepted.x: OBD-II continuously monitors emission performance and alerts the driver when a problem is detected.
accepted.tq: Identify the monitoring technology by its continuous diagnostic function.
accepted.sec: BS-VI technologies - DPF, SCR, OBD, RDE

accepted.s: Which technology was mandated as a shift for two-wheelers under BS-VI?
accepted.x: Electronic Fuel Injection was mandated for two-wheelers under BS-VI.
accepted.tq: Match the vehicle category with the specifically mandated technology.
accepted.sec: BS-VI technologies - DPF, SCR, OBD, RDE

accepted.s: Real Driving Emissions testing under BS-VI Phase 2 differs from conventional laboratory testing because it is conducted:
o: only on a dynamometer in a laboratory
only after a vehicle is scrapped
on actual roads under real driving conditions
accepted.x: RDE testing measures emissions on-road under real driving conditions and became applicable under BS-VI Phase 2 from April 2023.
accepted.tq: Use the expansion of RDE and the laboratory-versus-road contrast.
accepted.sec: BS-VI technologies - DPF, SCR, OBD, RDE

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about early Bharat Stage technologies is correct?
o: BS-I-era catalytic converters converted CO into CO2, while BS-II encouraged the shift from carburettors to multi-point fuel injection.
BS-I replaced catalytic converters with DPFs, while BS-II introduced SCR in all petrol vehicles.
BS-I mandated RDE, while BS-II mandated OBD-II.
BS-I and BS-II both required only battery-electric propulsion.
accepted.x: During the BS-I era, catalytic converters converted CO to CO2. BS-II promoted the shift from carburettors to multi-point fuel injection.
accepted.tq: Pair each technology with its correct Bharat Stage period.
accepted.sec: BS-VI technologies - DPF, SCR, OBD, RDE

accepted.s: Which of the following was a direct implication of BS-VI implementation for oil refineries?
o: They had to produce nationwide fuel containing 10 ppm sulphur.
They were permitted to increase fuel sulphur to 500 ppm.
They no longer needed to modify fuel-production facilities.
They had to stop producing petrol and diesel entirely.
accepted.x: Refineries had to upgrade their facilities to produce BS-VI fuel with a sulphur limit of 10 ppm nationwide.
accepted.tq: Connect the stricter fuel standard with the required refinery upgrade.
accepted.sec: Implications - refinery upgrades, vehicle cost, CAFE norms

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the economic implications of BS-VI adoption?
o: Vehicle prices fell because emission-control technology was removed.
Health benefits were absent because BS-VI regulates only noise pollution.
Only fuel prices changed; vehicle technology remained unaffected.
Vehicle prices rose because of new technology, while health savings partly offset the additional cost.
accepted.x: The introduction of advanced emission-control technologies increased vehicle prices, while improved public health produced offsetting social savings.
accepted.tq: Select the option that recognises both the immediate cost and the longer-term benefit.
accepted.sec: Implications - refinery upgrades, vehicle cost, CAFE norms

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the CAFE III draft:
1. It is the third draft.
2. It proposes fuel-efficiency norms for cars from April 2027.
3. It provides credits for ethanol, CBG and biofuels.
4. It proposes a flatter weight curve.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct features of the CAFE III draft.
accepted.tq: Handle a multi-feature policy statement by checking each provision separately.
accepted.sec: Implications - refinery upgrades, vehicle cost, CAFE norms

accepted.s: The CAFE III draft mentioned in the current policy context was dated:
accepted.x: The third CAFE draft was dated 16 July 2026. The following day, 17 July 2026, was associated with reporting on its targets and average vehicle weight.
accepted.tq: Distinguish adjacent dates attached to the draft and its reported details.
accepted.sec: Implications - refinery upgrades, vehicle cost, CAFE norms

accepted.s: Compared with the September 2025 proposal, the CAFE III draft relaxed its targets by approximately:
accepted.x: The CAFE III draft relaxed the targets by approximately 21% compared with the September 2025 proposal.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy percentage while rejecting nearby rounded distractors.
accepted.sec: Implications - refinery upgrades, vehicle cost, CAFE norms

accepted.s: The industry-average vehicle weight mentioned in relation to the CAFE III draft was:
accepted.x: The reported industry-average vehicle weight was 1,229 kg.
accepted.tq: Use the middle numerical option only after checking the exact reported figure.
accepted.sec: Implications - refinery upgrades, vehicle cost, CAFE norms

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the E20 rollout:
1. The E20 rollout was notified on 17 February 2026.
2. All States and Union Territories were to sell E20 with a minimum RON of 95 from 1 April 2026.
3. It replaced the 2021 E10 notification.
4. Concerns include mileage reduction, possible damage to older vehicles and the absence of an E0 choice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the E20 notification, its implementation, replacement of the earlier E10 notification and the associated concerns.
accepted.tq: Treat dates, coverage, supersession and policy concerns as separate components.
accepted.sec: Implications - refinery upgrades, vehicle cost, CAFE norms

accepted.s: Under the Vehicle Scrappage Policy, 2021, fitness-based de-registration is carried out through:
o: Automated Testing Stations and Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facilities
accepted.x: The policy provides for fitness-based de-registration through Automated Testing Stations and Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facilities.
accepted.tq: Match the policy mechanism with the institutions specifically designated for it.
accepted.sec: Allied measures - vehicle scrappage, PUC

accepted.s: A Pollution Under Control certificate is mandatory under:
accepted.x: A PUC certificate is mandatory under the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact legal instrument instead of choosing a broader environmental law.
accepted.sec: Allied measures - vehicle scrappage, PUC

accepted.s: Transport officers associated with the PUC system are trained at:
o: CPCB Delhi and CAQM Gurugram only
NITI Aayog Delhi and FCI Lucknow
accepted.x: Training is provided at the Automotive Research Association of India, Pune, and the Indian Institute of Petroleum, Dehradun.
accepted.tq: Use the institution-location pair rather than selecting a merely environment-related organisation.
accepted.sec: Allied measures - vehicle scrappage, PUC

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an NCR-associated measure listed in the context of vehicular pollution control?
accepted.x: CAQM, GRAP, NCAP and FAME for electric vehicles are associated measures for the NCR pollution-control context. The National Rural Employment Guarantee Programme is unrelated.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated programme among measures belonging to the same policy cluster.
accepted.sec: Allied measures - vehicle scrappage, PUC

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the planned next step in the Bharat Stage sequence?
o: BS-VIII, equivalent to Euro 6, planned for 2026–27
BS-VII, equivalent to Euro 5, planned for 2035–36
BS-VII, equivalent to Euro 7, planned for 2026–27
BS-V, equivalent to Euro 7, planned for 2026–27
accepted.x: BS-VII, planned for 2026–27, is expected to be equivalent to Euro 7.
accepted.tq: Check both the stage number and the corresponding Euro equivalence.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The reduction in fuel sulphur content from BS-II to BS-VI represents a fall from:
accepted.x: Fuel sulphur declined from 500 ppm under BS-II to 10 ppm under BS-VI, a major reduction over approximately fifteen years.
accepted.tq: Use the first-and-last values to identify the full magnitude of change.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly identifies both the first Euro-based Bharat Stage norm and the only skipped stage?
accepted.x: The first Euro-based norm under the Bharat Stage name was BS-I, introduced in 2000, and BS-V was the only stage skipped.
accepted.tq: Combine two “first/only” facts and reject options that shift either the year or stage.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
